# git shortlog

After this page you can turn a revision range into a contributor histogram with `git shortlog`, sort by commit count, switch between author and committer grouping, and avoid the quiet empty-output trap that bites scripts when stdout is not a tty.

## Thesis

`git log` is a stream of commits. Release notes, CODEOWNERS debates, and "who owns this tree this quarter" questions want a *rollup*: how many commits each person authored, optionally with the subject lines underneath. **`git shortlog`** is that rollup. It reads a revision walk (or a piped `git log --pretty=short`) and groups subjects under author names — or under committers when you ask for `-c`.

It is not a replacement for `git log`. It is a summarizer for the same history you already know how to range-limit and path-limit.

Verified below with **git 2.47.3**.

## What you get by default

```bash
git shortlog HEAD
```

Each author gets a heading with a parenthesized count, then an indented list of commit subjects:

```text
Alice Example (2):
      first
      second by alice
```

Subjects are the first line of each commit message. Order of authors is alphabetical by default; order of subjects under an author follows history (newest first within that author, matching the walk).

## Flags you actually use

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `-n` / `--numbered` | Sort authors by commit count (descending), not by name |
| `-s` / `--summary` | Counts only — drop the subject list |
| `-e` / `--email` | Append `<email>` to each name |
| `-c` / `--committer` | Group by *committer*, not author |
| `-w[<w>[,<i1>[,<i2>]]` | Wrap subject lines (width / indent1 / indent2) |
| `<revision-range>` | Same ranges as `git log` (`main`, `v1.0..v1.1`, `HEAD~10..`) |
| `-- <path>...` | Limit to commits that touch those paths |

The everyday release-notes shape is:

```bash
git shortlog -sn v1.2.0..v1.3.0
```

That prints a numbered summary of who authored commits since the previous tag. Add `-e` when two people share a display name and you need the address to tell them apart.

## Author versus committer

Every commit has **two** identities:

- **Author** — who wrote the change (preserved across rebase and cherry-pick by default).
- **Committer** — who last applied it to this history (changes on rebase, amend, cherry-pick).

`git shortlog` groups by author unless you pass `-c`. That matters when one person lands another person's patch:

```text
# Bob authored two commits; Alice was committer on one of them
git shortlog -sn HEAD
#      2  Alice Example
#      2  Bob Builder
#      1  Carol Coder

git shortlog -snc HEAD
#      3  Alice Example
#      1  Bob Builder
#      1  Carol Coder
```

Same five commits. Different story. For "who wrote the code," prefer author (`-sn`). For "who pushed it through," use committer (`-snc`).

## The non-tty gotcha

This is the footgun that empties CI logs and Makefile targets:

> If no revisions are passed on the command line and neither standard input nor standard output is a tty, a `--stdin` flag is assumed.

So this looks fine interactively:

```bash
git shortlog          # in a terminal: walks HEAD
```

but this is silent:

```bash
git shortlog > contributors.txt   # no range + redirected stdout → reads empty stdin
```

**Always pass an explicit revision** (usually `HEAD`, or a tag range) when you redirect or pipe:

```bash
git shortlog -sn HEAD > contributors.txt
git shortlog -sn v1.0..v1.1 | tee NOTES.txt
```

You can also feed it deliberately:

```bash
git log --pretty=short main | git shortlog -sn
```

## Path and range limits

Anything `git log` accepts as a range or path limiter works:

```bash
# Last two commits only
git shortlog -sn HEAD~2..HEAD

# Who touched src/ this release
git shortlog -sn v2.0.0..HEAD -- src/

# One file's recent authors
git shortlog -sne HEAD~50.. -- README.md
```

Path limits still attribute the whole commit to the author — shortlog does not fractionally score hunks. A commit that touches `src/` and `docs/` counts fully for both `-- src` and `-- docs` walks if you run them separately; it counts once in an unlimited walk.

## Lab: three authors, one committer twist

<!-- file: shortlog-lab.sh -->
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Recreate the verified shortlog demo (git 2.47.3).
set -euo pipefail
rm -rf /tmp/shortlog-demo && mkdir /tmp/shortlog-demo && cd /tmp/shortlog-demo
git init -b main
git config user.name 'Alice Example'
git config user.email alice@example.com

echo one > f.txt && git add f.txt && git commit -m 'first'
echo two >> f.txt && git commit -am 'second by alice'

GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Bob Builder' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=bob@example.com \
  GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Bob Builder' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=bob@example.com \
  bash -c 'echo three >> f.txt && git commit -am "bob feature"'

GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Bob Builder' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=bob@example.com \
  GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Alice Example' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=alice@example.com \
  bash -c 'echo four >> f.txt && git commit -am "bob again (alice commits)"'

GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Carol Coder' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=carol@example.com \
  GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Carol Coder' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=carol@example.com \
  bash -c 'echo five >> f.txt && git commit -am "carol tweak"'

echo "=== SHORTLOG LAB ==="
echo "--- shortlog HEAD ---"
git shortlog HEAD
echo "--- shortlog -sn HEAD ---"
git shortlog -sn HEAD
echo "--- shortlog -sne HEAD ---"
git shortlog -sne HEAD
echo "--- shortlog -snc HEAD (by committer) ---"
git shortlog -snc HEAD
echo "--- shortlog -sn HEAD~2..HEAD ---"
git shortlog -sn HEAD~2..HEAD
```

Running that script on the authoring box (**git 2.47.3**) produced:

```text
=== SHORTLOG LAB ===
--- shortlog HEAD ---
Alice Example (2):
      first
      second by alice

Bob Builder (2):
      bob feature
      bob again (alice commits)

Carol Coder (1):
      carol tweak

--- shortlog -sn HEAD ---
     2	Alice Example
     2	Bob Builder
     1	Carol Coder
--- shortlog -sne HEAD ---
     2	Alice Example <alice@example.com>
     2	Bob Builder <bob@example.com>
     1	Carol Coder <carol@example.com>
--- shortlog -snc HEAD (by committer) ---
     3	Alice Example
     1	Bob Builder
     1	Carol Coder
--- shortlog -sn HEAD~2..HEAD ---
     1	Bob Builder
     1	Carol Coder
```

Read the `-sn` versus `-snc` pair carefully: Bob *authored* two commits, but Alice was the *committer* on one of them, so Alice's committer count is 3 (her two authored commits plus Bob's second). The `HEAD~2..HEAD` range keeps only the newest two commits — Bob's second and Carol's — and drops Alice's earlier work.

## Mapping identities

People show up under whatever string is in `user.name` / `user.email` (or the `GIT_AUTHOR_*` overrides) at commit time. Typos create duplicate buckets:

```text
     40	Jane Doe
      3	jane doe
      1	JaneDoe
```

Fix forward with consistent `user.name` / `user.email`. For historical cleanup in a one-off report, `git shortlog` itself has no rename map — you post-process, or rewrite author fields with `git filter-repo` / `mailmap`. A `.mailmap` at the repo root *does* collapse identities for shortlog and log when present; keep it for long-lived projects with email churn.

```bash
# .mailmap example (committed)
Jane Doe <jane@example.com> <jane@old.example.com>
Jane Doe <jane@example.com> JaneDoe <jane@example.com>
```


## Building a release-notes fragment

A common release checklist ends with a contributor list and a subject dump for the changelog editor:

```bash
PREV=v1.4.0
CUR=v1.5.0

echo "## Contributors"
git shortlog -sn ${PREV}..${CUR}

echo
echo "## Changes by author"
git shortlog ${PREV}..${CUR}
```

Pair that with a conventional `git log --oneline ${PREV}..${CUR}` (or a `git log --pretty=format:...` that matches your changelog style) when you need hashes and full bodies. Shortlog answers *who*; log answers *what in order*.

For a single component inside a monorepo:

```bash
git shortlog -sn ${PREV}..${CUR} -- services/api/
```

That keeps mobile and docs churn out of the API release notes.

## Combining with other history tools

| Question | Tool |
|----------|------|
| Who authored commits in this range? | `git shortlog -sn` |
| What changed, in order? | `git log --oneline` |
| Who last touched *this line*? | `git blame` |
| Which commit introduced/removed this string? | `git log -S` / `-G` |
| Name a commit from nearby tags | `git describe` |

Shortlog sits at the "histogram over a walk" end of that table. It does not walk renames for you, does not search patch text, and does not annotate lines — hand those jobs to the tools built for them.

## Wrap width for pasted emails

When you paste shortlog into mail or a narrow terminal, long subjects collide with the indent. `-w` wraps:

```bash
# width 72, first indent 6, subsequent indent 9 (defaults are close to this)
git shortlog -w72,6,9 HEAD~20..HEAD
```

Most web markdown renderers ignore the wrapping and reflow anyway; use `-w` when the consumer is plain text.


## Empty ranges and merge commits

An empty range prints nothing and exits zero:

```bash
git shortlog -sn HEAD..HEAD    # no output
```

That is useful in scripts: treat empty stdout as "no contributors in range," not as failure.

Merge commits are included by default and credited to the merge author (usually the person who landed the PR). If you want a linear "patch authors only" view, exclude merges:

```bash
git shortlog -sn --no-merges v1.0.0..v1.1.0
```

`--no-merges` is a `git log` option that shortlog honors because it shares the same revision-walk machinery.

## Pitfalls

1. **Redirecting without a revision.** `git shortlog > out.txt` with no range reads stdin and prints nothing. Pass `HEAD` or a range.
2. **Assuming author == the person who pushed.** Rebases and GitHub "Merge pull request" buttons change the committer. Use `-c` when that is the question.
3. **Using shortlog as a blame substitute.** Counts are per commit, not per line. A 1,000-line drive-by and a one-line fix both count as one.
4. **Forgetting path limits on monorepos.** `git shortlog -sn v1..v2` across a huge tree mixes unrelated teams. Add `-- path/` for the component you care about.
5. **Pretty-format confusion.** `git shortlog` is its own pretty printer. Do not pass `--pretty=format:...` the way you would to `git log`; feed formatted log into shortlog via the pipe form if you need a custom walk.

## Summary

- `git shortlog` groups commit subjects under authors (or committers with `-c`).
- `-sn` is the release-notes histogram; add `-e` for emails.
- Always pass `HEAD` or a revision range when stdout is redirected — otherwise shortlog assumes `--stdin` and goes quiet.
- Author and committer tell different stories after rebase, amend, and cherry-pick; pick the flag that matches the question.
- Ranges and pathspecs work the same as `git log`.
